# Boundary transport gives actual variance matrices in mixed flux identities

This note extracts a consequence of the coupling proved in
`candidate 7278f286325c46c7`. It supplies actual
variance decompositions, stronger than an abstract positive-semidefinite
stress. It does not show that the mixed moment terms vanish or have a
useful common sign, and does not prove OC.

CORRECTION AND EXTENSION (2026-09-30): the integer-coordinate cap
covariance in (9) has a **minus** sign. The raw cap flux has outward
cut normal -v, so subtracting cap volume produces a **plus** section
flux before expanding its covariance. The prior plus-covariance display
was wrong even for genuine critical caps. An exact certificate and a
complete extension to arbitrary convex fibers, using bounded Borel
support-plane labels instead of facets, are proved in
`candidate 7127f9c7b67df7cb`.
Earlier audits of the old display do not certify this correction.

## 1. Quadratic differences equal transport variances

Let Pi couple nu to eta on a compact physical set, preserving each input
as its conditional output barycenter. Write w for the input, w' for the
output, and delta=w'-w. For every real symmetric matrix A,

    integral w^T A w d(eta-nu)
             = integral delta^T A delta dPi.                    (1)

Indeed expand w'=w+delta; the two cross terms have zero integral by the
row-barycenter identities, using the coordinate functions of w as tests.
If a compact parameter u is preserved by the coupling, (1) also holds
after multiplication by any bounded Borel function of u. Thus the
matrix-valued measure of quadratic differences, localized in u, is
positive semidefinite and is represented by the actual increments
delta delta^T. This conclusion does not follow from merely matching
first moments; the coupling is essential.

## 2. Every row stays in each supporting face through its input

Suppose the physical support is contained in a compact convex body C.
If N.w<=b on C and equality holds at an input w, then its output row
is concentrated on N.w'=b. The nonnegative random variable b-N.w'
has conditional mean b-N.w=0. Consequently N.delta=0 in that row.
This applies to every supporting hyperplane through the input; one
may use a countable dense subfamily of its normal cone to identify
the minimal face. For the argument below only a finite selected
supporting facet is needed, so no uncountable-null-set issue arises.

## 3. Shared polytopal facets receive consistent transport labels

Assume now that the actual finite-base body C is a polytope with positive
d-dimensional fibers K_p. List its nonvertical ambient facets as

    F_f={ (p,x) in C : a_f.p+u_f.x=b_f }, |u_f|=1.     (2)

Let eta be the sum of the fiber boundary-area measures, marked with the
unique continuous normal at almost every boundary point, and let nu be
the weighted cap-boundary measure from the normal-localized stress.
The coupling Pi from nu to eta preserves that continuous normal.

At every regular fiber-boundary point, at least one nonvertical facet
in (2) contains the point and has continuous normal equal to the marked
normal. Choose the smallest such facet index; this is a Borel rule.
Label an input row by that index f. Section 2 puts every output of
the row in F_f, and preservation of the continuous normal gives u_f
as its normal as well. Write Pi_f for the restriction to that label,
and nu_f, eta_f for its two marginals. Then

    sum_f nu_f=nu, sum_f eta_f=eta,
    integral (1,w) d(eta_f-nu_f)=0.                  (3)

The target eta_f need not use the same deterministic owner rule as
the source; its owner fractions are induced by the transport. This
difference is retained, rather than silently identifying the two.

Put W_f=eta_f-nu_f. Section 1 gives

    Q_f=integral w w^T dW_f
       =integral delta delta^T dPi_f >=0,
    Q_f (a_f,u_f)=0.                                (4)

The last equality holds because every increment stays in F_f. In blocks,
with B_f=integral p x^T dW_f,

    B_f^T a_f+Q_f^(xx) u_f=0,
    Q_f^(pp) a_f+B_f u_f=0.                         (5)

These are actual covariance kernels, including nontrivial owner ties.

## 4. Compatibility with cap traces and supporting-facet allocations

Write the original weighted boundary source as

    dnu=sum_j lambda_j alpha_j deta.

Here alpha_j equals the cap indicator at strict body traces. At an
inside supporting-facet coincidence alpha_j+sigma_j=1; at an outside
coincidence alpha_j=sigma_j, with both in [0,1]. The effective section
measure zeta_j uses sigma_j at that facet and full area on proper cuts.

Split each lambda_j alpha_j deta among source labels using the same
Borel owner rule of Section 3. This yields alpha_jf deta, with
sum_f alpha_jf=alpha_j, supported on the correct facets and continuous
normals. Its lambda-weighted sum is nu_f. The transported target eta_f
defines fractions omega_f with sum_f omega_f=1. Thus

    dW_f=(omega_f-sum_j lambda_j alpha_jf)deta.        (6)

The cap-section sigma_j and hence zeta_j have not changed. In particular
the inside and outside allocation identities are retained after summing
over facet owners. This is sufficient for the flux identities below.
We do not assert that these new owner fractions coincide with a previously
chosen multiplier certificate for unrelated facet deformations.

## 5. Exact mixed flux with the variance terms visible

Normalize cap j as H_j={a_j.p+v_j.x>=b_j}, |v_j|=1. Assume its effective
section measure belongs to a circuit group i and that

    lambda_j S_j=t_i rho_j,
    centroid(zeta_j)=(pbar_i,xbar_i),
    sum_(j in i) rho_j (b_j-a_j.pbar_i)=0.           (7)

These are the usual consistent section-stress conditions; they are
explicit hypotheses here. Define its full covariance matrix

    V_j=integral (w-wbar_i)(w-wbar_i)^T dzeta_j.

It is positive semidefinite and, since the section is in its cap plane,

    V_j(a_j,v_j)=0.                                 (8)

Write m_p=integral p dmu, m_x=integral x dmu for full mixed volume, and
m_pj,m_xj for the corresponding cap volume moments. Then

    d (m_p-sum_j lambda_j m_pj)
       =-sum_f Q_f^(pp) a_f -sum_j lambda_j V_j^(pp) a_j,          (9)

    (d+1)(m_x-sum_j lambda_j m_xj)
       = sum_f Q_f^(xx) u_f +sum_j lambda_j V_j^(xx) v_j.         (10)

Here every matrix in the displayed sums is an actual nonnegative
variance matrix. The vectors after multiplication by the corresponding
normals need not have a common direction or sign.

To verify (9), apply the fiberwise divergence theorem to the field x,
multiply by the fixed base p, and sum the fibers. For a cap, the cut
section has outward normal -v_j and v_j.x=b_j-a_j.p. With the consistent
facet allocations this gives

    d(m_p-sum lambda_j m_pj)
       =sum_f integral p(u_f.x)dW_f
                 +sum_j lambda_j integral p(b_j-a_j.p)dzeta_j.

Substitute u_f.x=b_f-a_f.p and use (3); the first term is
-sum Q_f^(pp) a_f. In the section term, expansion about its centroid
leaves S_j pbar_i(b_j-a_j.pbar_i)-V_j^(pp)a_j.
The first pieces cancel within each group by (7), proving (9).

For (10), test the field x(h.x), with divergence (d+1)h.x, for arbitrary
h in R^d. The same allocation identities give the vector formula

    (d+1)(m_x-sum lambda_j m_xj)
       =-sum_f B_f^T a_f -sum_j lambda_j C_j^T a_j,

where C_j is the base/continuous block of V_j. Equation (5) converts
the first terms to Q_f^(xx)u_f; (8) converts the second to
lambda_j V_j^(xx)v_j. This proves (10). All supporting-facet branch
terms are included in zeta_j; no full section is inserted at a tangent
cap by convention.

For d=1 the boundary and section measures are H_0 and the same one-variable
divergence identities apply. For a zero-dimensional base the pp blocks
are absent. Then the kernels in (4) and (8) imply separately
Q_f^(xx)u_f=0 and V_j^(xx)v_j=0, so (10) reduces to the familiar continuous
centroid identity.

## 6. Why variance positivity does not remove the mixed obstruction

Already on an actual shared interval facet, a nonzero mixed covariance
can satisfy all the transport requirements. Take P={0,1,2},
K_p=[p-1,p], and their upper endpoint normal u=1. The upper boundary
measure is eta_+=delta_(0,0)+delta_(1,1)+delta_(2,2). Let
nu_+=3 delta_(1,1). A coupling sends the three units at (1,1) equally
to the three endpoints. It preserves the normal, the input barycenter,
and lies in the ambient facet x-p=0. Its variance matrix is

    Q=2 [[1,1],[1,1]],
    Q(-1,1)^T=0,
    B=2, Q^(xx)u=2.

On the lower endpoint normal use the identity coupling of the full
lower boundary measure to itself. This gives the stated normal-localized
convex order on the entire actual boundary. It is not claimed to be a
critical-cap stress. Its role is the narrower exact demonstration that
even an actual normal-preserving martingale variance decomposition does
not make the body mixed term zero.

The new coupling therefore resolves the distinction between an abstract
PSD matrix and an actual variance representation. A further argument
must use the geometry of the critical caps and the universal selection
condition to control (9)--(10) or otherwise obtain the numerical depth
bound. Positivity alone does not supply that argument.
